standard.title: Technical Guidelines for Entertainment Establishments Compliance

notes.module_kind_justification: Same framework as GU83: a fixed requirement set in annexes, a risk class printed against each requirement, required actions per risk class, and an A-to-E grading formula. A report can state violation counts by class. Compliance module, with the same caveat as GU83 - the verdict is a GRADE, not a binary.
notes.age: Issued 10 December 2020, superseding a February 2020 edition. It is the OLDEST document in this group by more than four years, and the only one still carrying the pre-2023 Dubai Government / Dubai Municipality branding (GU83's version 2 change log records the logo swap that GU84 has not had). Contact addresses still point at esuggest.dubai.gov.ae and ecomplain.dubai.gov.ae, both superseded by the 04 Platform in GU83 and GU85. Treat GU84 as at risk of a silent re-issue and re-verify before sale.
notes.version_source: Version V 1.1 and issue date 10th December 2020 are taken from the page footer, which repeats them on all 25 pages. The cover page of GU84 carries NO version block at all - only the title and doc code - so unlike GU83 and GU85 there is no cover value to cross-check. The superseded issue date is printed as 'February 2020', a month with no day, so superseded_issue_date is stored as a partial date rather than invented as the 1st.
notes.risk_scale_differs_from_gu83: CRITICAL FOR THE DATA MODEL. GU84 and GU83 are the same framework with INCOMPATIBLE vocabularies on BOTH axes. GU84's risk-assessment outcomes are Low / Medium / High / Catastrophic; GU83's are Minor / Major / Critical / Catastrophic. GU84's severity axis is Negligible / Minor / Moderate / Major / Extreme; GU83's is Very Low / Low / Medium / High / Very High. GU84's probability axis starts at 'Rare/Remote'; GU83's starts at 'Very Unlikely'. The words overlap but mean different things across documents: 'Minor' is a risk OUTCOME in GU83 and a SEVERITY INPUT in GU84; 'Medium' is a severity input in GU83 and a risk outcome in GU84. A single shared severity enum across guideline modules will silently mis-map GU84 findings into GU83 semantics and vice versa. failure_severity below therefore carries GU84's OWN lowercase label, and source_risk_label carries it verbatim. Severity must be namespaced per standard, not global.
notes.grading_differs_from_gu83: GU84 grades A to E with E as the worst; GU83 grades A to F with F as the worst and no E. The thresholds also differ: GU84 grade A requires ZERO violations of every class, while GU83 grade A tolerates 1 to 2 Minor. 'Grade A' therefore does not mean the same thing in the two documents and must never be displayed as a cross-guideline score. Both grading tables share the same undecidable '&/or' combinator problem.
notes.gu83_annex_pointers_came_from_here: GU84's section 10 annex references are internally CORRECT: toys to Annex 5, low voltage to Annex 8, detergents to Annex 10, biocides to Annex 11, indoor air to Annex 2, non-drinking water to Annex 3, noise to Annex 4. GU83's section 10 cites exactly these same annex numbers, but GU83's Part E renumbers everything (toys are Annex 6 there, indoor air Annex 3, and so on). GU83's body text was evidently copied from GU84 and its annex pointers were never renumbered. This confirms the GU83 off-by-one is a copy-paste defect rather than a reading error on our side.
notes.annex_numbering_gaps: GU84's Part E contains Annexes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10 and 11. Annexes 6, 7 and 9 do not exist in this document. The numbering is inherited from a shared master annex library (where 6 = food contact materials, 7 = cosmetics, 9 = health supplements in GU83's scheme), and GU84 simply omits the ones entertainment establishments do not deal in. The gaps are not missing pages: page numbering is continuous and the document is complete at 25 of 25.
notes.two_level_tables: GU84's annex tables are TWO-LEVEL in a way GU83's are not. Many rows print a Requirement with the Risk cell EMPTY, and the rows beneath elaborate it with their own risk classes. Those header rows are marked is_group_heading and carry no severity. GU84 never states this structure in words - it is read off the layout - so the grouping is flagged as an inference. The section 4.6 model as sketched has no place for it: checklist_items would need a self-referential parent_item_id, or the headers get scored as failures they were never meant to be.
self_contradictions: Annex 1 prints 'Availability of suitable cleaning materials.' twice, once as Medium and once as High. Same requirement, two risk classes, four rows apart. Both are retained; the second is set to failure_severity 'unknown' because preferring either would be a guess that changes a grade.

Annex 2 prints 'Presence of suitable ventilation mechanism in pump rooms.' as a group heading with no risk AND again as a Medium item eight rows later. Whether that is one requirement or two is not determinable from the document.

Annex 3 is titled 'Non drinking water system requirements' but three of its items are explicitly about DRINKING water tanks (opaque, closed and sealed, easily cleaned drinking water tanks). Section 10-E also scopes it to 'Non drinking water system compliance'. Serving these items under a non-drinking-water heading is the document's error, not ours.

Annex 1 item A1.114 is not a checkpoint at all: the Requirement cell reads ':TG14, TG15, TG16, TG17, TG18, 19, TG20, AND TG21' - a bare list of guideline references, with 'TG' missing from '19' - yet it carries a risk class of High and would therefore be scored. It is preserved verbatim and flagged; it cannot be inspected against as written.

Section 10-A and 10-B both point at Annex 1 for two different subject areas (public health and hygiene, and public and operational safety), so GU84 has no way to report the two separately even though its own contents page lists them as distinct compliance areas.
notes.unit_conflict_with_gu83: GU84 requires ashtrays 25 feet from entrances; GU83 requires 7.62 metres. These are the same distance expressed in different units - 25 ft = 7.62 m exactly - so there is no substantive conflict, but any cross-guideline comparison must normalise units before flagging a discrepancy, and a client reading both documents will see two different numbers.
notes.numbering: Annex requirements are printed as unnumbered table rows. All item_no values (A<annex>.<row>) are positional and assigned by this extraction. Item TEXT is verbatim, including the document's own errors.
notes.response_type: yes_no_na is this extraction's inference, as in GU83. The document prints only a requirement and a risk class.

matrix.note: Rows are 'Probability of repetition', columns are 'Severity of the potential risk'. The cell value is the RISK ASSESSMENT class used by section 9 grading. NOTE the vocabulary differs from GU83 on every axis - see notes.risk_scale_differs_from_gu83.

risk_module.note: Each requirement violation assessed to its risk based on business activity type, and upon final findings grade of establishment estimated.

grading.source_quote: Establishment's violations to the environmental health requirements shall affect overall grade as per below formulas settled as per management decisions: Where highest level of compliance score A grade, in descending order to grade E.
grading.evaluation_order: E first, then D, C, B, A - the first grade whose condition is satisfied wins.
unresolved: The combinator is printed as '&/or', which is not a decidable operator - the same defect as GU83.

Grade A is cleanly defined here (zero of everything) but no band mentions Catastrophic except E, so an establishment with 1 Catastrophic and nothing else lands in E, which is coherent; an establishment with 0 of everything lands in A, also coherent. GU84's table is more nearly self-consistent than GU83's - the A/B overlap does not occur here - but the '&/or' problem alone still blocks automatic scoring.
Do not implement automatic grading without written clarification from DM. Emit violation counts by class.

obligations.cadence_note: Routine inspection frequency is driven by the premise grade; the grade-to-frequency mapping is not published.
obligations.source_quote: Routine: scheduled visit based on premise grade.

obligations.trigger_event: remarks detected upon previous findings risk
obligations.source_quote: Follow-Up: scheduled visit according to remarks detected upon previous findings risk.
Complaint: Enforced unexpected visit scheduled upon incidences received.

obligations.trigger_event: management decision, memo or case investigation
obligations.source_quote: Management Order: Enforced expected visit scheduled upon management decisions, memos or during case investigation.

obligations.trigger_event: quality issues or field status changes
obligations.source_quote: Random: Non-Forced unexpected inspection according to quality issues, or could be determined on the status and changes in the field.

obligations.applies_to: Consumer products, non-drinking water and indoor air
obligations.source_quote: Sampling: Enforced expected visit scheduled specifically for consumer products and/or non-drinking water and/or indoor air sample site measurement and collection for the purpose of testing and determine environmental health conditions, however, it may processed in conjunction with previous types of visits.

obligations.cadence_note: Named as a monitoring mode; no frequency given.
obligations.source_quote: Notification and case investigation with establishment remotely via self-inspection or during investigation visit.
